content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias as prices fall below forecasted levels.", "Sentiment spikes with positive values correlate with forecast overshoots, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast window.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment shows prolonged negative signals, indicating model underconfidence in downward trends.", "Model forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 3–5 days, particularly during sharp downward corrections.", "High sentiment volatility (e.g., alternating 1.00 and 0.00) correlates with forecast instability and wider error margins.", "Forecasts with low historical volatility show higher mean-reversion tendency, while high volatility periods exhibit forecast drift.", "Sentiment-driven corrections are often faster than model-adjusted forecasts, suggesting sentiment leads price action in short-term cycles.", "Model forecasts should be adjusted downward when sentiment shows sustained negative values, especially if historical price trends are declining."]}
